name: Glozel
hook: A French field yielded 'Neolithic' tablets in an unknown script; critics soon called them forgeries.
claim: Antonin Morlet, building on finds by the Fradin family, argued that pits at Glozel held an early Neolithic necropolis of a civilization unknown to science: inscribed clay tablets in an unattested alphabetic script, ceramic 'idols', engraved stones and bones.

claimed_age.label: Early Neolithic; c. 4000-3500 BC per Reinach (1926)
claimed_age.basis: Morlet: 'haute époque néolithique' by typology, no Roman or Celtic finds (S1); no absolute dating. Reinach (The Times, 1926) dated idols and inscriptions to about 4000-3500 [BC] (quoted in S13).

accepted_age.label: Glozelian objects non-authentic; TL ages disputed
accepted_age.basis: Publisher of the 2023 monograph: documents 'considérés comme non authentiques' (S12). Antiquity's translator (S3) deemed genuine only glass-kiln debris and a few flint chips. 1974 TL was 'preliminary', disputed.

orthodoxy_at_claim.label: No script was accepted for Neolithic western Europe; Reinach's view that the Palaeolithic lasted to c. 5000 BC was called 'unorthodox'.

unambiguous_signal.note: Objects were plainly man-made, but their age was disputed from the outset: Reinach set 'Aegean' Neolithic idols beside 'degenerate Magdalenian' engravings (S13).

documented_context.note: S1: the first oval pit was found and destroyed before Morlet's regular digging began; no stratigraphic record by a trained excavator appears in sources read.

multiple_dating_methods.note: Age rested on typology and the absence of Roman or Celtic finds; no absolute dating was used.

multiple_labs.note: No laboratory analysis supported the original claim; S1 relays typological arguments only.

professional_recovery.note: S1 relays the dig as Dr Morlet's, aided by the Fradin family; no trained archaeologist is named as directing it.

peer_reviewed_report.note: The claim reached the Académie only as a two-page relay of Morlet's report (S1); no refereed technical report by the proponents was found.

material_accessible.note: Reinach reported finds 'ascertained last summer at Glozel' (1926, S13); the 1927 International Commission worked on the ground and examined earlier finds (S11).

independent_teams.note: No independent team corroborated the claim in sources read. The 1927 International Commission (S11) investigated for the critics; a pro-Glozel 1928 committee is unverified.

proponent_stake.note: Accounts of paid excavation rights and a paying family museum were not found in any source read here.

objections.text: The finds were dug by Dr Morlet and the Fradin family without recorded stratigraphy, so their context cannot be checked.
objections.raised_by: Critics; lesson restated by the 2023 monograph
objections.outcome_note: 1983 state test pits sought intact deposits to check and found none ('infructueuse'), so the original context cannot now be tested (S8).

objections.text: Engravings, perforations and borings on the Glozel stones were made with metal tools, not by ancient techniques.
objections.outcome_note: Not overturned in sources read; consistent with the 2023 monograph's view that the finds are not authentic (S12).

objections.text: Nearly everything at Glozel was forged; only glass-kiln bricks, crucibles, glass and a few flint chips were genuine, all but the flints of late date.
objections.raised_by: Vayson de Pradenne and Dussaud; list per Antiquity's translator
objections.outcome_note: The 2023 monograph's publisher calls the documents 'non authentiques' (S12); TL on some ceramics remains disputed (see below).

objections.text: TL on inscribed tablets, urns, idols and other ceramics gave a preliminary date within 700 BC-AD 100, far too young for a Neolithic age.
objections.raised_by: McKerrell et al. (who offered TL as proof against forgery)
objections.outcome_note: No later source read dates Glozelian objects to the Neolithic; the TL ages themselves remain disputed (next objection).

objections.text: The TL ages might be unsound: a forger could have irradiated modern pieces to mimic age, and dose rates needed refining.
objections.outcome_note: Zimmerman's zircon result was not read; the 1983-90 programme ran dosimetry to refine TL (S8); its 2023 TL chapters were not read.

objections.text: State test pits at Glozel found no intact archaeological deposits, and three related findspots showed only medieval and modern occupation, no Glozelian remains.
objections.outcome_note: Reported in the 1995 summary (S8 p. 1); both reports are chapters of the 2023 monograph (S9).

status_note: The claimed Neolithic civilization with its own script lost professional support by 1927-30 and never regained it. The 2023 monograph deems the finds non-authentic; some still reject this (S9), and early TL ages remain disputed.
what_settled_it: Antiquity's 1927 critique (S13) and the International Commission's report (Dec 1927, S11) came first; by 1930 Antiquity called the fraud exposed, citing 'official reports' as 'categorical proofs of forgery' (S3). TL from 1974 reopened only whether some objects are old.

timeline.event: Enigmatic objects are found at Glozel's 'Champ des Morts' (Allier), opening a dispute over their authenticity and meaning.
Salomon Reinach backs the finds in The Times (27 Sept), dating idols and inscriptions to about 4000-3500 BC.
Morlet's report is relayed to the Académie des Inscriptions: 'haute époque néolithique', no Roman or Celtic finds.
The International Commission's report on its fieldwork and on earlier finds appears on 23 December (Revue anthropologique).
Champion, of the Saint-Germain museum workshops, reports that engravings and borings on the stones were made with metal tools.
Science News-Letter headline: 'Glozel Alphabet Called Fraud'.
Antiquity prints Vayson de Pradenne's 'The Glozel Forgeries', treating the fraud as exposed.
TL on tablets, urns, idols and other ceramics gives a 'preliminary date' within 700 BC-AD 100; the authors call the objects genuine.
Antiquity prints 'Thermoluminescence and Glozel: a plea for caution'; the TL team replies with 'a plea for patience'.
Zimmerman runs zircon-grain TL to test whether samples could have been artificially irradiated to fake an old age.
State test pits find no intact deposits at Glozel; 1983-84 work at three related findspots finds only medieval and modern occupation.
Full results of the 1983-1990 programme are published (Guilaine & Miallier dir.); the publisher calls the finds non-authentic.

falsifier: Status would change if securely stratified Neolithic material with Glozel-type script were excavated and dated by several methods. TL/OSL with controlled dosimetry showing inscribed tablets fired in antiquity would shift failure_mode from hoax toward misinterpretation.

confidence_note: Fields rest on passages read (S1-S3, S5, S8 p. 1, S9, S11-S13, S16). Unread: commission report, S7, S8 conclusions, monograph chapters. Legal-case details unchecked, so omitted.
corrections: Brief: 'a later French ministry review (1990s)'. Clarification: fieldwork was 1983 test pits (no intact deposits) and 1983-84 work at related sites (medieval/modern only), summarized in 1995 (S8); full results 2023 (S12).
notes: Glozel yielded tablets, 'idols', urns and bones, but the original digging left no intact deposits to check (S8). Antiquity's translator deemed genuine only glass-kiln debris and a few flint chips (S3). The 1974 TL range (700 BC-AD 100) was 'preliminary'; forgery by artificial irradiation was tested (S16) and dose rates were studied in 1983-90 (S8). Whether later TL (S7) gave mixed ages, as the brief says, was not checked, so the draft's correction of 'mixed' was withdrawn. year_claimed 1925 (Morlet's first publication) is UNVERIFIED; the earliest public claim read is Reinach's 1926 letter (S13). Police and court episodes of 1928-32 are omitted as unchecked.

UNVERIFIED: year_claimed 1925 (Morlet and Fradin's first fascicle) was not located; the earliest public claim read is Reinach's 1926 Times letter (S13).
Unread: Mejdahl 1980 (S7, Wiley 403), the 'plea for caution' (S14) and the 2023 TL chapters, so the TL objection stays 'unresolved' and the 'mixed ages' correction was withdrawn.
Not verified: the pro-Glozel 1928 Comite d'etudes, the 1928 police raid and the 1929 police report; omitted, so independent_teams is coded 'no' on read sources only.
Dropped Garrod and Regnault from key_critics (no read source); 'Antoine' changed to 'A.' for Vayson de Pradenne, as the first name was not verified.
Declined: confidence 'low'. After revision each field rests on a passage read and the gaps are listed here, so 'medium' is kept.

D19 re-rating 2026-09-23: unchanged — refuted fits: metal-tool engraving, forgery findings (1927-30) and TL ages far too young for the Neolithic positively contradict the claim; disputed TL leaves only whether some objects are old.
